# DSP Architecture: WARPR (working title)

**CRITICAL CONTRACT:** This specification is immutable during implementation stages. Implementation (Foundation, Shell, DSP, GUI, Validation) follows this exact architecture. Deviations require amending this file first.

**Generated by:** Stage 0 Research (research-planning-agent), 2026-11-11
**Inputs (read-only contracts):** `creative-brief.md`, `parameter-spec.md` (135 parameters, LOCKED), `mockups/v9-ui.yaml`, `mockups/v9-integration-checklist.md`, `mockups/v9-PluginEditor.h/.cpp`, `mockups/v9-CMakeLists.txt`
**Referenced by:** Stage 1 (Planning/Foundation/Shell), Stage 2 (DSP), Stage 3 (GUI), Validation
**Plugin type:** Instrument (IS_SYNTH, MIDI in, stereo out) - sample-based wave-warp synthesizer
**Complexity tier:** 6 (DEEP research) - largest plugin in the factory
**Rename safety:** Parameter IDs contain no plugin name. All product-name-dependent strings live in ONE header (`Source/PluginIdentity.h`: product name, preset directory, preset extension, WebView2 data folder, state tags). State tags `WARPR_UI_STATE` and container magic `WRPR` are FROZEN even after a rename (they are part of the saved-state wire format). `PLUGIN_CODE Wrpr` / `PLUGIN_MANUFACTURER_CODE Vstf` in `v9-CMakeLists.txt` are the AU/VST3 identity: they MUST be decided before the first public build (changing them later orphans saved DAW projects).

---

## Architecture in One Page (decisions at a glance)

| # | Decision | One-line justification |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Per-note voice = {N unison oscillators -> sum -> ONE filter -> ONE amp ADSR}** | Matches brief signal path; filter/ADSR cost scales with polyphony (32), not with polyphony x unison (256) |
| 2 | **Oscillator pipeline runs natively at the oversampled rate** (read -> warp -> shaper at OS x fs), summed per voice, then ONE polyphase half-band IIR decimator per voice | Sample reading IS the upsampler (no input up-filter); phase-domain warps (FM/PD/sync) are only alias-controllable at the OS rate; decimator count = voices (32), not oscillators (256) |
| 3 | **Anti-aliasing = oversampling (user 1x-8x) + first-order ADAA on every static nonlinearity + BLEP on hard steps + mip-mapped band-limited source with speed-aware level choice** | ADAA alone cannot cover time-varying/phase-domain modes; OS alone needs 8x for hard clip/folds; combined, default 2x behaves like ~8x on static shapers (verified by test A1/A2 thresholds) |
| 4 | **All phase-domain warps are expressed as an additive read-position offset `DeltaP = Lc * Delta(theta)`** where `Lc = fileSR / midiToHz(rootNote)` (one root-period of the sample) and `theta` is a per-oscillator note-cycle clock | One mechanism makes PD / bend / sync / FM / PM / self-FM / cross-mod work on arbitrary sample material, in Classic AND Granular source modes, with zero latency |
| 5 | **Sample data is an immutable ref-counted `SampleData` (planar float + octave mip pyramid + peaks) published by atomic pointer swap; retired objects are freed only on the message thread** | Audio thread never allocates/locks/frees |
| 6 | **State = custom binary container (`WRPR` magic): APVTS+UI-state XML, then one binary sample blob (24-bit FLAC or raw float32)** | No base64 bloat, host-state friendly, embedded sample survives projects |
| 7 | **Modulation = table-driven LFOs (two-sided 4096-cell tables built off-thread) + matrix evaluated per 32-sample chunk with per-sample linear interpolation; sources sample-accurate from the transport** | Exact analytic shapes (UI/DSP agreement), cheap, polyphonic where needed |
| 8 | **Filters = 34 real topologies in 9 families sharing TPT building blocks; analytic response comes from the same coefficient code as the audio path** | Response display is the real DSP, not a drawing |
| 9 | **Granular = per-oscillator `GrainEngine` with preallocated pools (CLASSIC 2/ch, LOOP 2 xfading/ch, CLOUD <=20/ch), run at min(OS,2)x and up-sampled to OS** | Bounded CPU, click-free, phase-domain warps apply per grain |
| 10 | **No `juce::dsp::Limiter`** (hidden 4:1 @ -10 dBFS compressor). Master safety = custom knee soft-clip with ADAA + NaN/inf guard | House lesson |

## Core Components

Namespace `warpr`. Files under `Source/DSP`, `Source/Parameters`, `Source/State`, `Source/Backend` unless noted. Every DSP class is GUI-free and unit-testable without JUCE processors (explicit `prepare(double fs, int maxBlock)`).

### C1. SampleData / SampleStore / SampleLoader / SampleCodec
- **JUCE Class:** `juce::AudioFormatManager` (`registerBasicFormats()` -> WAV, AIFF, FLAC; MP3 not required), `juce::AudioFormatReader`, `juce::AudioBuffer<float>`, `juce::FlacAudioFormat` (embedding), `juce::ReferenceCountedObject`, `juce::ThreadPool`. Module `juce_audio_formats`.
- **Purpose:** Decode sample off the audio thread, build an immutable `SampleData` {name, fileSampleRate, numChannels (1 or 2; >2 channels: first two), planar float channels, **mip pyramid** (octave-decimated band-limited copies, up to 8 levels), **peaks** (<=2048 min/max pairs mono mix), `isDefaultWave`, `seamInfo`}.
- **Parameters Affected:** sampleStart, sampleEnd, rootNote, playMode (indirect); non-parameter: embedded sample.
- **Configuration:** Mip level k is low-passed at 0.5/2^k cycles/sample (63-tap Kaiser half-band FIR cascade, >=100 dB) and stored decimated; total memory ~2x source. Build on the loader thread (`ThreadPool` job). Soft length cap 10 min (documented, see Ambiguities A8). Default built-in wave: 2048-sample single cycle (additive saw, 64 harmonics 1/n, peak 0.9), `fileSampleRate = 2048 * midiToHz(60)` so that rootNote 60 maps exactly one cycle to one note period; regenerated deterministically, never stored in state (only `isDefaultWave=1`).
- **Publication:** `SampleStore` holds `std::atomic<SampleData*> pending`; audio thread `exchange(nullptr)` at block start and adopts it (see C20 `RetireList`).

### C2. SampleReader (interpolation + mip selection)
- **JUCE Class:** Custom. (juce::Interpolators are 4-point max and have no mip awareness.)
- **Purpose:** Fractional-position stereo read. 8-tap Kaiser-windowed sinc, 512 sub-phases, linear interpolation between phase rows (stopband > 80 dB); optional 4-point Hermite "draft" path for the CPU governor. **Mip level** chosen from the instantaneous *effective* speed `rho_eff = |dP_warped/dn_base|` (finite difference of the warped read position, smoothed), blended between two adjacent levels in the octave where `rho_eff > 1`; no mip needed for `rho_eff <= 1`.
- **Parameters Affected:** rootNote, transpose, fineTune, direction, loopMode, sampleStart, sampleEnd.
- **Configuration:** Region playhead `P` (double, source frames); `RegionFold(P')` maps any read position into [start,end]: Forward Loop = wrap with **seam crossfade**, Ping-Pong = reflect, One-Shot = clamp-start / silence-after-end. Seam crossfade (loop removed from the spec, so policy is internal): length `X = 0` for flagged single-cycle or when the seam discontinuity < 0.002 (value) and slope mismatch small; else `X = min(L/4, 20 ms)`; during the last X frames output = equal-power blend of `s(P)` and `s(start + (P - (end - X)))`, and the playhead wraps to `start + X`. Computed O(1) when start/end change (audio thread safe, no allocation).

### C3. PhaseWarp (families F1, F2, F5 - phase-domain)
- **JUCE Class:** Custom (`PhaseWarp::offset(mode, a, A, B, theta, modState) -> DeltaCycles`).
- **Purpose:** Produce the read-position offset in cycles for bending (H group), phase & time (44-50), sync (51-53), and FM/PM/Self-FM/Cross (54, 55, 58, 59).
- **Parameters Affected:** warpMode, warpAmount, warpParamA, warpParamB, modOscSource, modOscRatio, warpMix.

### C4. AmpWarp (families F3, F4 - amplitude-domain)
- **JUCE Class:** Custom. `Adaa` helpers (C5).
- **Purpose:** Memoryless and low-state amplitude shapers: vertical bends (4-6, 8, 10-13), folds (15-24), distortions (25-43), AM/RM (56, 57).
- **Parameters Affected:** same as C3.

### C5. Adaa kernels + FastMath
- **JUCE Class:** Custom (`juce::dsp::FastMathApproximations` supplies tanh/sin/cos Padé but with unspecified error; we use our own paired `f`/`F1` implementations so that `F1' == f` to 1e-5, verified by test).
- **Purpose:** First-order antiderivative antialiasing `y[n] = (F1(x[n]) - F1(x[n-1])) / (x[n] - x[n-1])`, fallback `f((x[n]+x[n-1])/2)` when `|dx| < 1e-5`. Per-channel `x_prev` state, parameters read at the current sample for both `F1` evaluations (consistent under smoothing). Closed-form `F1` for hard clip, cubic, rational soft-clip, tanh (log-cosh, numerically stable form), atan, exp/diode curves, power laws, polynomials, Chebyshev (recurrence of integrals), sine, triangle/linear fold (piecewise quadratic), rectifiers, quantizer staircase (piecewise linear). 3-point Simpson quadrature ADAA ("numerical ADAA") for functions without closed form (Soft Fold blend, non-integer Chebyshev fold).

### C6. ShaperEngine (A/B transfer-curve waveshaper)
- **JUCE Class:** Custom. `juce::var`/`juce::JSON` on the message thread for wire format.
- **Purpose:** Evaluates the user curve (A, B, morph) via 4097-point LUTs + 4097-point antiderivative LUTs (Hermite cubic reconstruction using `f` as the derivative of `F1`), ADAA1 on the lookup. Off-thread `ShaperCurveBuilder` converts control points (Fritsch-Carlson monotone cubic or linear) to LUT+F1 (double-precision cumulative integral), applies Symmetric (odd mirror of x>=0 half) / Asymmetric mode, publishes via triple-buffer swap.
- **Parameters Affected:** shaperEnable, shaperCurveSelect (editor target only - not read by DSP), shaperMorph, shaperPreset (UI/model only), shaperSymmetry, shaperMix.

### C7. GrainEngine
- **JUCE Class:** Custom. `juce::Random` NOT used on the audio thread (shared state); per-voice xorshift32 seeded by note counter (deterministic offline renders).
- **Purpose:** CLASSIC / LOOP / CLOUD grain scheduling from preallocated pools, scan ramp, windows from a shared shape LUT.
- **Parameters Affected:** playMode, grainMode, grainPosition, grainScan, grainScanDist, grainScanLoop, grainScanKey, grainSize, grainShape, grainVariation, grainSpread, grainReverse, grainDensity (+ sampleStart/End, direction, rootNote, transpose, fineTune).

### C8. ModOsc
- **JUCE Class:** Custom (`juce::dsp::Oscillator` is wavetable, not BLEP, no ratio-lock/phase read-out; rejected).
- **Purpose:** Modulator for FM/PM/AM/RM/Cross: Sine (fast poly), Triangle (BLAMP-corrected), Saw / Square (polyBLEP at OS rate), **Sample** (second `SampleReader` playhead at `rho * modOscRatio`).
- **Parameters Affected:** modOscSource, modOscRatio.

### C9. FilterEngine (34 types, 9 families)
- **JUCE Class:** Custom topologies on TPT (zero-delay-feedback) building blocks. `juce::dsp::StateVariableTPTFilter` is the reference/foundation for the 12 dB SVF sections (we reimplement its recurrence in `TptSvf` to add notch/peak/shelf/allpass taps and per-chunk coefficient interpolation, and unit-test against the JUCE class for LP/BP/HP equivalence). `juce::dsp::DelayLine<float, juce::dsp::DelayLineInterpolationTypes::Lagrange3rd>` for comb. `juce::dsp::FilterDesign` is NOT used for the audio filters.
- **Purpose:** Per-voice stereo filter, type switch crossfade, drive, key tracking, mix, analytic response.
- **Parameters Affected:** filterEnable, filterType, filterCutoff, filterResonance, filterDrive, filterMorph, filterKeyTrack, filterMix.

### C10. AmpEnvelope (single ADSR)
- **JUCE Class:** Custom (`juce::ADSR` has no retrigger-from-level exponential segments, no per-sample times; rejected).
- **Parameters Affected:** ampAttack, ampDecay, ampSustain, ampRelease.

### C11. LfoShapeTable + LfoEngine + ModMatrix + TransportClock
- **JUCE Class:** `juce::AudioPlayHead::getPosition()` (ppq, bpm, isPlaying, time signature); `juce::var/JSON` message-thread parsing. Module `juce_audio_basics`, `juce_core`.
- **Purpose:** 10 shape tables, 10 LFO engines (FREE/RETRIG/ENV/MONO, dir, Hz/Sync, smooth), matrix with src 1..10 -> dst parameterId, depth 0..1.
- **Parameters Affected:** lfo1..10 Mode/Dir/Sync/Rate/Phase/Smooth (GridX/GridY = UI-only), all destinations in the matrix.

### C12. UnisonOsc + WarprVoice + WarprSound + WarprSynth
- **JUCE Class:** `juce::Synthesiser` (subclass `WarprSynth`: overrides `noteOn`, `noteOff`, `handlePitchWheel`, `handleController`, `handleSustainPedal`, `renderVoices`), `juce::SynthesiserVoice` (`WarprVoice`), `juce::SynthesiserSound` (`WarprSound`, `appliesToNote()==true`). Module `juce_audio_basics`.
- **Purpose:** Voice allocation (Poly/Mono/Legato), stealing, glide, unison, pitch bend, sustain pedal, sample-accurate note starts (Synthesiser sub-block splitting), 32 voices + 2 fade-out "ghost" slots.
- **Parameters Affected:** voiceMode, polyphony, unisonVoices, unisonDetune, unisonSpread, glideTime, bendRange.

### C13. HalfbandIIR + OsDecimator + OsUpsampler
- **JUCE Class:** Coefficients from `juce::dsp::FilterDesign<float>::designIIRLowpassHalfBandPolyphaseAllpassMethod(transitionWidth, stopbandDb)` (public API, verified present in the local JUCE 8.0.15 `juce_Oversampling.cpp`); run by our own polyphase all-pass loops. `juce::dsp::Oversampling<float>` (`filterHalfBandPolyphaseIIR`, `isMaxQuality=false`) is used for base-rate-in/base-rate-out nonlinear sections (filter-internal 2x for Res/Dist/Scream/RingMod, optional master-safety) where its standard Up->process->Down usage fits.
- **Purpose:** Per-voice decimator cascade (8x = 3 stages) fed directly with OS-rate oscillator output; Granular up-sampler (S->OS).
- **Parameters Affected:** oversampling.

### C14. MasterStage
- **JUCE Class:** `juce::SmoothedValue<float, juce::ValueSmoothingTypes::Linear>` (dB-domain smoothing), custom DC blocker (one-pole HP ~5 Hz), custom knee soft-clip safety (ADAA1), NaN/inf guard.
- **Parameters Affected:** masterGain.

### C15. VizAnalyzer + `VizFifo.h`
- **JUCE Class:** `juce::AbstractFifo` (SPSC; `WarprVizFifo` from `v9-PluginEditor.h` moved verbatim to `Source/DSP/VizFifo.h`).
- **Purpose:** Fills `WarprVizFrame` once per ~33 ms on the audio thread (see UI Backend section).

### C16. ParameterLayout / ParamSnapshot
- **JUCE Class:** `juce::AudioProcessorValueTreeState`, `juce::AudioParameterFloat/Int/Bool/Choice`, `juce::NormalisableRange<float>` (`setSkewForCentre`), `juce::AudioParameterChoiceAttributes().withAutomatable(false)` (verified present in JUCE 8.0.15), `juce::ParameterID{ id, 1 }`.
- **Purpose:** One macro/table-driven definition (`WARPR_PARAM_TABLE(X)`) generates: IDs, layout (exact spec order: Sample, Granular, Warp, Shaper, Envelope, Filter, LFO1..10, Global), `ParamSnapshot` (raw `std::atomic<float>*` pointers cached once), and the editor relay tables (v9 `WARPR_*_PARAMS` macros are generated from the same table in Stage 3 to prevent drift).

### C17. StateIO + PresetManager
- **JUCE Class:** `juce::MemoryBlock`, `juce::MemoryOutputStream/InputStream`, `juce::XmlElement`, `juce::ValueTree`, `juce::File`, `juce::FileChooser` (async), `juce::FlacAudioFormat`. Module `juce_audio_formats`, `juce_data_structures`.
- **Purpose:** Binary container read/write, migration (`warprStateVersion`), `.warpr` preset files (same container), user preset directory, `presetStep()` file iteration.

### C18. UiBackendImpl
- **JUCE Class:** Implements `WarprUiBackend` (declared in `v9-PluginEditor.h`). Message-thread model objects + `std::atomic<uint32_t>` revision counters.
- **Purpose:** Everything the editor needs; see "UI Backend Implementation Plan".

### C19. Test support (`Source/Tests/`, target `WARPR_Tests`, EXCLUDE_FROM_ALL)
- Offline renderer (pattern from `plugins/KICKR/Source/Tests/OfflineRender.*`), global `operator new/delete` counting hooks to prove zero audio-thread allocations, NaN/inf/DC/discontinuity scanners, FFT alias meter (`juce::dsp::FFT`, test-only).

### C20. LockFreeSwap<T> + RetireList (shared infrastructure)
- **JUCE Class:** `std::atomic<T*>`, `juce::ReferenceCountedObjectPtr`, `juce::AbstractFifo`.
- **Purpose:** The only cross-thread publication primitive for big objects (SampleData, ShaperLuts, LfoShapeTables, ModMatrixSnapshot). Message thread allocates and `publish(newPtr)`; audio thread `acquire()` at block start (single `exchange`); the *previous* object is pushed into a retire FIFO (preallocated capacity 64) drained by the editor/message-thread timer, so `delete` never runs on the audio thread. If the FIFO is full the audio thread keeps the old object (no publication consumed) - back-pressure, never a free.

## Processing Chain

### Per-instrument

```
MIDI in --> WarprSynth (allocation, stealing, glide state, bend, pedal, mod wheel)
              |
              +--> TransportClock (ppq, bpm, play state; once per block)
              +--> LfoEngine global instances (FREE / MONO)  -> ModSourceBuffers
              +--> ParamSnapshot (all 135 atomics read once per block)
              |
   up to 32 (+2 ghost) WarprVoice  --each renders in 32-sample base-rate chunks-->  voice stereo out
              |
      sum of voices (stereo)
              v
        MasterStage: DC blocker -> masterGain (smoothed, dB) -> safety knee soft-clip (ADAA1) -> NaN/inf guard
              v
        stereo out  --> peaks, band energies, transient detector --> VizAnalyzer --> WarprVizFifo (~30 Hz)
```

### Per-voice (one note; `N = unisonVoices` oscillators)

```
note + transpose + fine + bend*range + glide  --> pitch_semis (per voice, per chunk)
mod sources (LFO1..10) via ModMatrix -----------> modulated parameter values (per chunk, linear-interpolated per sample)

 for each unison oscillator i = 0..N-1  (own playhead P_i, note clock theta_i, detune_i, pan_i, PRNG)
 ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  [ClassicReader | GrainEngine]           (OS-rate native)       [Granular: S = min(OS,2)x then OsUpsampler to OS]
        |  read position P_i  --(+ DeltaP from PhaseWarp)-->  SampleReader(P') per channel (L,R or mono)
        v
  PhaseWarp  (F1/F2/F5: adds DeltaP = Lc*Delta(theta,a,A,B,modOsc) BEFORE the read)  ---- warpEnable/warpMix
  AmpWarp    (F3/F4: shapes the read value, ADAA1)                                    ---- dry/wet = warpMix
        v
  ShaperEngine  (A/B LUT morph, ADAA1)                                                 ---- shaperEnable/shaperMix
        v
  pan_i / spread (equal-power balance) --> accumulate into the voice OS-rate stereo bus (x 1/sqrt(N) compensation)
 ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
        v
  OsDecimator (polyphase half-band IIR cascade, OS -> 1x)       ONE per voice (stereo)
        v
  per-voice DC-block (5 Hz) + sanity guard (non-finite or |y|>64 -> kill voice)
        v
  FilterEngine (drive -> type -> cutoff*keytrack -> resonance/morph -> mix) [type-switch crossfade 10 ms]   ---- filterEnable
        v
  AmpEnvelope (ADSR) * velocity law * voice level
        v
  voice stereo out  (+ playhead/level snapshot for viz)
```

**Sample-rate domains:** base `fs` (host) | OS rate `OS*fs` (oscillator pipeline: read, warp, shaper) | granular source rate `min(OS,2)*fs` (grain reads + per-grain phase warps) | filter/ADSR/voice sum/master at base rate. Filters with internal nonlinearity (Res LP/HP, Dist LP, Scream, Ring Mod) run their own local 2x (`HalfbandIIR`) regardless of OS.

**Where the oversampling parameter acts:** `oversampling` (1x/2x/4x/8x) selects the OS factor **latched per voice at note-on**. Changing it mid-note never touches sounding voices (no reset, no click); new notes use the new factor. (Offline/bounce quality is therefore "set before playing".)

**Order and bypass rules**
- `warpEnable=false` -> warp stage skipped (read at unwarped P). `shaperEnable=false` -> shaper skipped. `filterEnable=false` -> filter skipped. Disabling ramps the stage mix over 5 ms (never a hard switch).
- `warpMix`: `y = lerp(dry, warped, mix)` where *dry* is the unwarped read (second read only when mix<1 and the mode is phase-domain).
- Warp -> Shaper -> Filter -> ADSR order is fixed (brief).
- Sample-as-modulator reads the sample a second time inside the oscillator (not an extra voice).

### Mono-source optimisation
If `SampleData.numChannels == 1`, warp+shaper run on one channel and the result is duplicated before panning (halves oscillator cost). Stereo sources run L and R independently with **shared position/offset** (identical `DeltaP`) so stereo imaging is not decorrelated by the phase warps; amplitude-domain stages keep per-channel ADAA state.

## System Architecture

### File I/O System

**File types supported:** `.wav`, `.aif`, `.aiff` (UI filter in `v9-PluginEditor.cpp`); `AudioFormatManager::registerBasicFormats()` also decodes FLAC/OGG where compiled in - not advertised. 8/16/24/32-bit int and 32-bit float. Multi-channel files: first two channels.

**Loading strategy:** `UiBackendImpl::loadSampleFile(File)` (message thread) enqueues a `juce::ThreadPool` job (1 worker, low priority): `createReaderFor` -> read into `AudioBuffer<float>` -> normalise nothing (preserve level) -> build mips + peaks + seam info -> `SampleStore::publish()` -> `Revision::sample++` -> sample is also encoded for state (FLAC24 / float32) *lazily at getStateInformation time* (on the host's state thread, not at load).

**JUCE classes:** `AudioFormatManager`, `AudioFormatReader`, `AudioBuffer<float>`, `FlacAudioFormat` (+ `AudioFormatWriterOptions`; JUCE 8.0.15 writer API must be checked at Foundation: the legacy `createWriterFor` overloads are deprecated), `ThreadPool`.

**Thread safety:** Decoding and mip building never on the audio thread or the message thread (except `setStateInformation`, see State Persistence). Audio thread receives the new `SampleData*` through `LockFreeSwap`. Sounding voices keep their own ref (`ReferenceCountedObjectPtr` copied at note-on; the **retire list holds an extra reference**, so the last release can never happen on the audio thread). On swap, voices still sounding on the old sample finish naturally (old data kept alive), new notes use the new sample - no click, no stuck reads.

**Error handling:** Unreadable/invalid file: the previous sample is kept and a native `juce::AlertWindow::showMessageBoxAsync` explains the failure (the `warprSample` event has no error field in the contract). Zero-length files are rejected; NaN/inf values are scrubbed to 0 at load so they can never reach the audio thread. A saved preset can never reference a missing file because the sample is embedded.

---

### Multi-Output Routing
Not applicable. Single stereo output bus (`BusesProperties().withOutput("Output", stereo, true)`; **no input bus** - pattern #4). Mono-only host layouts are not supported (reject in `isBusesLayoutSupported`).

### MIDI Routing

- Input: note on/off (velocity), pitch wheel, CC1 (mod wheel - stored; has no destination in the contract, see Ambiguity A2), CC64 sustain, CC123/120 all-notes/sound-off, channel 1-16 omni. No MIDI out. No MPE.
- Pitch bend: `bendRange` choice -> {2,12,24} semitones; wheel 0..16383 -> [-1,1] -> slewed 3 ms.
- **Voice modes:** Poly (up to `polyphony` voices), Mono (single voice, last-note priority, note stack, retrigger envelope from current level), Legato (single voice, overlap = no retrigger, glide only). `glideTime` works in all three (Poly: each new voice starts at the *last played pitch* and glides to its note).
- **Stealing (Poly):** (1) same note, (2) quietest voice in release, (3) oldest sounding voice. Stolen voices fade 3 ms in a ghost slot while the new note starts in its own slot.
- **Velocity law (fixed, no parameter exists):** `g = 0.25 + 0.75 * v`. Mod wheel/note number/velocity are *not* matrix sources in the v1.0 wire format (src is 1..10).
- Sample-accurate starts: `juce::Synthesiser::renderNextBlock` splits the block at MIDI timestamps and calls `renderVoices(buffer, start, num)`; WarprSynth advances global LFOs/transport in step with those sub-blocks and voices internally chunk to <=32 base samples.
- Sustain pedal and all-notes-off are implemented in `WarprSynth::noteOff/handleSustainPedal` (not via the base-class sustain map because Mono/Legato need the note stack).

### State Persistence

**Contents (everything must round-trip bit-exactly):**
1. APVTS state: all 135 parameters (`juce::ValueTree`/XML).
2. `<WARPR_UI_STATE warprStateVersion="1" lfoCount="N">` child: per-LFO shape JSON (`<LFO index json>`), mod matrix JSON, shaper curves JSON `{A,B}` (wire formats exactly as in parameter-spec "Non-Parameter State" 2-6). Stored as JSON strings inside XML attributes (canonical writer: fixed key order, `%.9g`) to guarantee UI/DSP identity.
3. Embedded sample (binary, outside the XML).
4. `presetName` attribute.

**Container (`getStateInformation` and `.warpr` files, identical):**
```
u32  magic  = 'WRPR'
u32  containerVersion = 1
u32  xmlByteCount        ; followed by UTF-8 XML (APVTS root + WARPR_UI_STATE)
u32  sampleBlobByteCount ; 0 = default wave / none
blob:
  u8  codec        ; 0 = float32 planar raw, 1 = FLAC 24-bit (lossless for <=24-bit sources; float32 raw otherwise)
  u8  numChannels  ; 1 or 2
  u8  flags        ; bit0 = isDefaultWave
  f64 fileSampleRate
  u64 numFrames
  u16 nameByteCount ; UTF-8 name
  u32 payloadByteCount ; payload
```
Why not base64 in XML: +33% size and a multi-MB attribute string through `XmlElement`; why not a ValueTree `MemoryBlock` property: same copy cost and no streaming. Little-endian explicit (`ByteOrder::littleEndian*`) for cross-platform presets.

**setStateInformation:** validates magic; falls back to `juce::AudioProcessor::getXmlFromBinary` (plain XML, no sample) and then to "empty/invalid -> keep defaults + default wave". Decodes the sample **synchronously** (FLAC decode + mip build; ~0.2 s for 60 s stereo) so offline renders immediately after load are correct; publishes through the same swap. `apvts.replaceState()`; then bumps `Revision::uiState/sample/preset/shaperCurves/filterResponse`. Unknown newer `warprStateVersion` -> load what is understood, never crash.

**Migration:** `warprStateVersion` integer; v1 is current. Rule (CORRUPTR lesson): removed parameters are never re-indexed; choice lists are append-only; dead entries retained.

**Size policy:** 24-bit FLAC ~50-60% of PCM; a 30 s stereo 48 kHz sample ~ 4-5 MB. Samples > 64 MB decoded are loaded but a one-time warning dialog tells the user the project state will be large (Ambiguity A8).

**Presets:** `.warpr` = container. Directory `<userApplicationData>/<PluginIdentity::companyDir>/<product>/Presets`. `presetStep(+-1)` cycles the sorted file list; factory presets (later) = `BinaryData` containers listed first. `presetSaveDialog/LoadDialog` use async `FileChooser`. `getPresetName()` returns the loaded name or "Init".

### UI Backend Implementation Plan (`WarprUiBackend`)

`PluginProcessor` owns `UiBackendImpl backend; WarprUiBackend& getUiBackend() { return backend; }` and `juce::AudioProcessorValueTreeState apvts`.

| Interface member | Implementation | Thread |
|---|---|---|
| `vizFifo()` | Returns the `WarprVizFifo` owned by `VizAnalyzer`; audio thread `push()` once per 33 ms (counter in samples: `fs/30`) | audio -> message |
| `revision(r)` | `std::atomic<uint32_t>[5]`; `fetch_add(1, relaxed)` | any |
| `getUiStateJson()` | Serialises `UiModel` (`lfoCount`, `lfoShapes[]`, `modMatrix[]`, `shaperCurves{A,B}`) to the exact wire format with `juce::JSON::toString(var, true)`; model is message-thread owned | message |
| `setLfoCount(n)` | Clamp 1..10; updates model; publishes `lfoCount` (atomic int) to LfoEngine (LFOs >= n are idle, their matrix routes ignored) | message |
| `setLfoShapeJson(i,json)` | Parse -> `LfoShapeDesc` -> `LfoTableBuilder` builds the two-sided 4096-cell table (+ metadata) -> `LockFreeSwap<LfoShapeTable>[i].publish()`; model updated. Coalesced by the UI (80 ms debounce already in v9) | message |
| `setModMatrixJson(json)` | Parse -> validate `dst` against the parameter table (unknown ids dropped, `depth` clamped 0..1) -> compile to `ModMatrixSnapshot` (flat arrays: per-destination source masks/depths, destination param index, kind) -> `LockFreeSwap` | message |
| `setShaperCurveJson(id,json)` | Parse -> `ShaperCurve` model (**does NOT bump `Revision::shaperCurves`** - echo avoidance per checklist) -> `ShaperCurveBuilder` (LUT+F1) -> swap into `ShaperEngine` slot A or B; sets `shaperPreset` parameter to *Custom* (via `apvts.getParameter("shaperPreset")->setValueNotifyingHost` with gesture begin/end) if it was not already Custom | message |
| `getShaperCurveJson(id)` | Canonical JSON of the model curve | message |
| `shaperReset(id)` | Curve -> identity `(-1,-1),(0,0),(1,1)` smooth; rebuild; **bump `shaperCurves`**; preset param -> Custom | message |
| `shaperNormalize(id)` | `y *= 1/max|y|` over the sampled curve (control points scaled); rebuild; bump `shaperCurves` | message |
| (listener) `shaperPreset` change | `apvts.addParameterListener`: callback only sets an atomic dirty flag + target curve id; message-thread timer applies `ShaperPresetLibrary::generate(preset, curveSelect)` -> model -> rebuild -> bump `shaperCurves` (never builds on the host/audio thread) | host -> message |
| `loadSampleFile(file)` | See File I/O; bumps `Revision::sample` (and `uiState` is NOT bumped) | message + worker |
| `getSampleDisplay()` | Reads `SampleStore::current()` (ref-counted, safe), returns `name`, `numChannels`, `sampleRate`, `numSamples`, `peaksMinMax` (precomputed, <=2048 pairs) | message |
| `computeFilterResponse(db,n)` | Reads current raw values of the 8 filter params (atomics) and calls `FilterResponse::magnitudeDb(type, cutoff, res, drive, morph, fs, freqs)` for n=256 log-spaced 20 Hz-20 kHz points, clamped to [-48,+24] dB. Uses the same coefficient generators as the audio path; no shared mutable state | message |
| `revision(filterResponse)` | Bumped from a `juce::AudioProcessorValueTreeState::Listener` on the 8 filter params (callback is a single atomic increment: wait-free, legal on any thread) and on `prepareToPlay` (sample-rate change) | any |
| `getPresetName / presetStep / presetSaveDialog / presetLoadDialog / openSettings` | `PresetManager`; Settings = small native `juce::DialogWindow` (non-parameter app settings in `juce::PropertiesFile`: oscillator budget, interpolation quality, CPU governor on/off) | message |

**`warprViz` frame producers (all from the audio thread, ~1 push/33 ms):**

| Field | Source |
|---|---|
| `low` | one-pole LP @ 200 Hz of the master mono sum -> rectified -> follower (att 5 ms, rel 120 ms), normalised by running max (slow, 8 s) |
| `high` | 2nd-order HP @ 4 kHz -> same follower chain |
| `rms` | 300 ms RMS follower of master sum; `0` below -90 dBFS (organism becomes static circles) |
| `transient`, `tseq` | spectral-flux surrogate: HP@2 kHz energy derivative vs 50 ms adaptive threshold, refractory 60 ms; `tseq++` per hit, `transient` = normalised strength for that frame else 0 |
| `tang` | spectral-centroid surrogate = zero-crossing-rate of the HP@500 Hz signal over the last 20 ms -> log map 200 Hz..12 kHz -> 0..2pi (no FFT on the audio thread) |
| `theta`, `r` | block energies of Mid and Side: `theta = atan2(S, M)`, `r = clamp(sqrt(M^2+S^2)*k, 0, 1)` |
| `peakL/R` | max |sample| since last push, after master gain/safety clip |
| `voices[]` | per active voice: `pos` = unwarped playhead / numFrames of oscillator 0 (Granular: read position of the most recently spawned grain on channel L), `level` = ADSR * velocity; numVoices <= 32 |
| `lfoPhase[0..9]` | Global LFO: its phase; voice LFO: phase of the most recently started voice; **-1** if index >= lfoCount, or LFO is unused by the matrix, or (voice LFO) no active voice |

The tap point for the analyzers is the master sum *after* voice filters (the "post-warp" bus in the contract is read as "the sound after the whole warp chain"; recorded as Ambiguity A10).

## Parameter Mapping

**Source of truth:** `parameter-spec.md` (135 parameters: 62 Float, 5 Int, 5 Bool, 63 Choice; 115 automatable + 20 non-automatable `lfoNGridX/Y`). IDs, ranges, defaults, skews and order are NOT repeated here; this section binds each parameter to its DSP target, rate class and smoothing.

**Read pattern (audio thread):** `ParamSnapshot` caches `std::atomic<float>*` from `apvts.getRawParameterValue(id)` once in the constructor (pointer table indexed by enum, no string lookups in `processBlock`). At each block start the processor copies all values into a plain `ParamBlock` struct (135 loads, relaxed). Choices/Ints/Bools are converted with `static_cast<int>(value + 0.5f)`.

**Rate classes**

| Code | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `G` | Global, read once per block |
| `V` | Per-voice; evaluated every 32-sample chunk together with modulation; linearly interpolated per sample where the consumer is per-sample |
| `N` | Latched at note-on (or at grain spawn / next trigger) |
| `D` | Discrete: changes are crossfaded (`DiscreteSwitchFade`, 8-10 ms, both variants run for the fade, new variant state reset) |
| `UI` | Not read by DSP (editor/model only) |

**Smoothing strategy (by class)**
- Gain-like / mix / amount floats: `juce::SmoothedValue<float, Linear>` 10 ms (20 ms for master/ADSR sustain), advanced per sample in the voice (value pre-computed per chunk with ramp end-points, so no per-sample object calls: `v += dv`).
- Frequency-like (filterCutoff, modOscRatio): **multiplicative (log-domain) smoothing**, 15 ms; filter coefficient `g=tan(pi*fc/fs)` recomputed every 8 samples from the interpolated log-frequency (fast tan approximation, max error 1e-4).
- Pitch-like (rootNote, transpose, fineTune, bend, glide): one slew in the semitone domain (5 ms for transpose/fine/root edits, 3 ms bend, glide per `glideTime`).
- Enables/bools: 5 ms mix ramp. Mode choices (`warpMode`, `filterType`, `playMode`, `grainMode`, `modOscSource`): `D` crossfade. `oversampling`, `unisonVoices`, `voiceMode`: `N` (new notes only).
- **Modulation** is added in the normalised domain after smoothing: `norm' = clamp(norm_smoothed + sum_s depth_s * (2 v_s - 1), 0, 1)`, then `range.convertFrom0to1` (skew respected; e.g. cutoff modulates in the log-skewed domain, matching the UI rim). Int destinations round to nearest after conversion (can step; documented).

### Modulation destination rules (matrix)
- A destination may be any Float/Int parameter ID in the table above; the editor decides which knobs offer drops. Choice/Bool destinations (and unknown IDs) are dropped when the matrix is parsed.
- **Per-voice (V):** evaluated per voice per chunk with that voice's own LFO values (Retrig/Env LFOs) or the shared value (Free/Mono LFOs).
- **Global (G, masterGain):** uses the global instance value (voice LFOs contribute their mean over active voices - documented, rarely used).
- **Latched (N: polyphony, unisonVoices, glideTime):** sampled at note-on.
- **LFO-on-LFO** (`lfoNRate/Phase/Smooth` as destinations): LFOs are evaluated in index order 1..10 each chunk; a source with index < destination index is same-chunk, otherwise it contributes with a **one-chunk delay** (no algebraic loops, deterministic).
- Depth is unipolar 0..1 in the contract (no negative depth; inversion is done by drawing the shape).
- Matrix snapshot is a flat structure-of-arrays (<= 256 routes); evaluation cost O(routes x active voices) per chunk.

---

## Algorithm Details

### A. Anti-Aliasing Strategy (decision and justification)

**Decision:** Layered, not either/or.

1. **User-facing oversampling (1x/2x/4x/8x)** of the *oscillator pipeline* (sample read + warp + shaper), latched per voice. It is the only mechanism that covers *every* mode, including time-varying and phase-domain ones (PD, sync, FM/PM/Self-FM/Cross, quantisers, bit/SR crush, dynamic fold).
2. **First-order ADAA** inside every static nonlinearity that has a closed-form antiderivative (or an integrated LUT: the shaper). It improves the alias floor of hard clip / folds / tanh-class shapers by roughly the amount of one OS octave-doubling at ~2 evaluations per sample; combined with the default 2x it brings static shapers to the quality region of naive 8x (acceptance tests A1/A2 in plan.md make this a measured claim, not an assumption). Rejected: second-order ADAA as default (needs 2 samples of history, half-sample extra delay, ill-conditioned branches; reserved as an optional "high quality" path for Linear Fold/Hard Clip if tests demand it).
3. **BLEP/BLAMP** for the few hard discontinuities that are *generated* (Hard Sync reset step, Flip polarity edges, Wave Skew wrap ramp, PWM edges, ModOsc saw/square/triangle): step magnitude known analytically at the OS rate.
4. **Band-limited source:** octave mip pyramid; level selected from the *speed after warping* (`rho_eff`) so that content stays below base Nyquist before nonlinear processing; blended between adjacent levels to avoid timbre steps. This is what stops "sample played 3 octaves up" from aliasing before any warp.
5. **Decimation:** polyphase half-band IIR (min-phase, ~>=96 dB stopband, designed by `FilterDesign::designIIRLowpassHalfBandPolyphaseAllpassMethod`), zero reported latency (instrument; the ~1 ms group delay at note start is part of the voice).

**Why not ADAA-only:** cannot apply to phase-domain/stateful modes, and the oscillator reads would still alias. **Why not OS-only:** hard clip and 8-fold folds need >= 8x for clean results; 8x on 256 oscillators is not affordable, so static shapers must get "free" suppression from ADAA at 2x-4x. **Why decimators per voice not per oscillator:** decimation is linear; `sum_i D(x_i) = D(sum_i x_i)`, so the unison sum is decimated once (256 -> 32 decimators worst case).

**Known limits (documented, tested):** Chebyshev Harmonic with 8 harmonics at 1x still aliases audibly above 3 kHz fundamentals; Bitcrush/SR Reduction alias *by design*; FM/Cross with index > 8 at 1x. The UI OS select is the user's remedy.

### B. Sample Reader, Loop Regions, Pitch

- `rho = 2^((pitch_semis - rootNote)/12) * fileSR / fs` (source frames per base sample). `Lc = fileSR / midiToHz(rootNote)`. Pitch clamp so that `rho <= 256`; beyond that the oscillator mutes (no garbage).
- Playhead `P` is `double`; per OS sample `P += dir * rho / OS` (Granular: per grain). Region fold per C2. One-Shot ends: oscillator marks `ended`; the voice forces a 5 ms release when all its oscillators ended.
- **Start phase of unison oscillators:** all at `sampleStart` (samples keep identical attacks; the detune provides the chorus). Exception: regions shorter than 4096 frames (single-cycle-like) spread start phases by the golden ratio (0.618...) so unison is not phase-locked.
- Mono-note-clock: `theta_i += f_note_i / (fs*OS)` (double, wrapped to [0,1)); `f_note_i = midiToHz(pitch_semis + detune_i)`.

### C. Phase-Domain Framework (the core idea)

All phase-domain warps compute a *cycle offset* `Delta(theta)` (in cycles of the sample's root period) and read at

```
P' = RegionFold( P + dir * Lc * Delta )
```

`Delta = g(theta) - theta` for remap-style modes (so `g(theta)` is the warped cycle phase: `g(0)=0, g(1)=1` => continuous), `Delta = I * integral(m)` (FM), `I * m` (PM, Cross), `I * y[n-1]` (Self FM). Because `P` advances exactly `Lc` per note cycle (`rho/OS * OS/fs`-consistent), `theta` is the cycle clock **independent of loops, direction and granular grain restarts**, so the same offset function works in Classic and per-grain in Granular. Modes whose `g(1) != 1` produce a read-position jump at the cycle wrap; a `SeamBridge` (0.25-base-sample linear ramp of the *output*, tracked per oscillator) removes hard steps while preserving the intended discontinuity timbre; for periodic material (single-cycle waves, tuned samples with correct `rootNote`) these jumps are continuous anyway.

`rho_eff` for mip selection = `|rho/OS + dDelta*Lc/dn|` smoothed (one-pole 0.2 ms), computed from consecutive `Delta` values (no analytic derivatives required).

**Parameter convention for the mode tables:** `a` = warpAmount (0 = neutral), `A` = warpParamA (default 0.5), `B` = warpParamB (default 0). `sm(x)=x^2(3-2x)`, `tri(t)=1-|2t-1|`, `e = 1 + a*(1+7A)`. "Neutral at a=0" holds for every row. Constants are starting values for tuning in Stage 2; the **structure** (domain, formula family, parameter roles, aliasing treatment) is the contract. Where A or B is "-" the knob has no effect in that mode (documented to the UI via `WarpModeInfo`, Ambiguity A5).

### D. Warp Mode Families and the 60 Modes

**Family map (shared infrastructure)**

| Family | Domain | Shared code | Modes |
|---|---|---|---|
| **H** Phase-map bends | read position (offset of `g(theta)`) | `PhaseWarp::remap(g)` + SeamBridge | 0,1,2,3,7,9,14 |
| **V** Amplitude power/asym bends | value, ADAA1 closed-form power laws, DC-blocked | `AmpWarp::power*` | 4,5,6,11,12,13 |
| **VT** Cycle-aware amplitude | value x function of `theta`, BLEP edges | `AmpWarp::thetaGate` | 8,10 |
| **FOLD** Static folds | value, ADAA1 (closed-form F1) | `Fold::{triangle,sine,reflectN,...}` | 15,16,17,18,19,20,21,22,24 |
| **DYN** Dynamic fold | value + envelope follower | `Fold` + `EnvFollower` | 23 |
| **CLIP** Static distortions | value, ADAA1 closed form | `Clip::*` | 25-37 |
| **RECT** Rectifiers | value, ADAA1 | `Rect::*` | 38,39,40 |
| **QNT** Quantisers/rate | value/time staircase, ADAA1 staircase / S&H | `Quant::*` | 41,42,43 |
| **PHM** Phase & time maps | read position | `PhaseWarp::remap(g)` | 44,45,46,47,48,49,50 |
| **SYN** Sync | read position + BLEP | `PhaseWarp::sync` | 51,52,53 |
| **MOD** Modulation | read position (FM/PM/Self/Cross) or value (AM/RM) | `ModOsc` + `PhaseWarp::pm` / `AmpWarp::am,rm` | 54-59 |

**Static-shaper wrapper (CLIP/FOLD/RECT):** `y = lerp(x, shaped(Dx)/norm, min(1, 20a))` with drive `D = 1 + a*(1 + 15A)` (`A` = drive range), output normalised to ~+-1, DC removed by the voice DC blocker (and by analytic offset removal where the shape is asymmetric). `B` = shape-specific secondary (below). The `min(1,20a)` ramp guarantees exact identity at `a=0`.

#### Wave Bending (0-14)

| # | Mode | Family | Definition | A / B | Alias handling |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | Bend Positive | H | `g = theta^e` | A range / - | OS |
| 1 | Bend Negative | H | `g = 1-(1-theta)^e` | A range / - | OS |
| 2 | Bend Symmetric | H | `g = 0.5(2 theta)^e` (theta<.5), `1-0.5(2-2 theta)^e` otherwise | A range / - | OS |
| 3 | Bend Asymmetric | H | first half exponent `e`, second half `e2 = 1+8aB` | A range 1st half / B 2nd half amount | OS |
| 4 | Asym Positive | V | positive lobe `x^p`, `p = 1/(1+3a(0.5+A))`, negative lobe unchanged (even harmonics), DC removed | A strength / - | ADAA1 (`F1 = x^(p+1)/(p+1)`) |
| 5 | Asym Negative | V | mirror of 4 on the negative lobe | A strength / - | ADAA1 |
| 6 | Asym Bidirectional | V | positive lobe `p+ = 1/(1+3aA)`, negative lobe `p- = 1/(1+3aB)` (independent) | A positive depth / B negative depth | ADAA1 |
| 7 | PWM | H | compress cycle into window `w = 1-0.95a`, offset `o = A(1-w)`: `g = clamp((theta-o)/w, 0, 1)`; outside window the read position holds | A window position / B edge softness (0..25% of w, smoothstep) | OS + BLEP at window edges if B=0 |
| 8 | Flip | VT | `y = x * s(theta)`, `s=-1` for the last fraction `a` of the cycle (start offset A), edges smoothed over `B*10%` of the cycle | A region offset / B edge softness | OS + BLEP polarity step |
| 9 | Mirror | H | mirror point `m = 1-0.5a`; `g = theta` for theta<=m, `2m-theta` after (time-reversal of the tail) | A - / B apex rounding | OS + SeamBridge |
| 10 | Wave Skew | VT | add ramp lean: `y = (x + k r(theta))/(1+k)`, `k=2a`, `r = 2theta-1` morphed to exp curve by A (0.5 = linear) | A ramp curvature / B ramp pivot (blends toward `sin(2 pi theta)` lean) | OS + BLEP at wrap |
| 11 | Wave Stretch | V | peak-flattening compander `sgn(x)(1-(1-|x|)^p)`, `p=1+3a` | A knee blend toward linear / - | ADAA1 closed form |
| 12 | Wave Compress | V | `sgn(x)|x|^p`, `p = 1+3a` (low-level compression) | A threshold blend / - | ADAA1 |
| 13 | Wave Expand | V | `sgn(x)|x|^(1/p)`, `p=1+3a` (low-level expansion) | A threshold blend / - | ADAA1 (Simpson near 0 where slope is infinite) |

#### Modulation (54-59) - `ModOsc` (C8)

Modulator `m(n)` in [-1,1]: Sine/Tri/Saw/Square at `f_mod = ratio * f_note` (phase accumulator double; polyBLEP/BLAMP at OS rate) or **Sample** (second reader, playhead `P_m = P0 + ratio*(P-P0)` => Granular: uses the grain engine's scan position; mips apply to the modulator read as well). `I` = index.

| 59 | Cross Mod | MOD | mutual PM: carrier `Delta_c = I*m_prev`, modulator read `Delta_m = I*y_prev`, with `modOscSource` (Sample recommended) | A index ratio carrier:modulator / B mutual feedback | OS; both readers mip-aware |

**Warp state machine:** `WarpModeTable[mode] = { family, kernelFn, usesModOsc, usesTheta, aLabel, bLabel, neutralAtZero }`. Mode change = `D` crossfade: outgoing kernel keeps running for 10 ms with frozen parameter targets while the incoming starts with reset state. `WarpModeInfo` (labels) is a compile-time table shared with Stage 3 (Ambiguity A5).

### E. Shaper

- **Model:** `ShaperCurve{ interp: smooth|linear, points[] }` for A and B, x in [-1,1], first/last at -1/+1 (wire format identical to spec). Symmetric mode: only x>=0 half used and mirrored odd (`f(-x) = -f(x)`); Asymmetric: full list.
- **LUT build (message thread):** 4097 uniform samples over [-1,1]; smooth = monotone cubic Hermite (Fritsch-Carlson) - the same algorithm as the UI; linear = piecewise. `F1` = running Simpson integral in double, stored as float with the Hermite reconstruction `F1(x) = H(F1_i, F1_{i+1}, f_i, f_{i+1}, t)`.
- **Audio:** input clamped to [-1,1] (soft-limited at 1.5 by `tanh` before clamp to avoid cliffs from FM/folds overshoot), `y = ADAA1(lookup)`; fallback to midpoint lookup when |dx|<1e-5; morph via linear blend of both curves' `f` and `F1`; A/B LUT swaps crossfade 10 ms.
- **Presets (`ShaperPresetLibrary`, 9 entries):** Soft Sat (tanh(2.5x)/tanh(2.5), 9 pts smooth), Hard Clip (4 pts linear: (-1,-1),(-.5,-1),(.5,1),(1,1)), Tube (asymmetric tanh bias, 11 pts smooth), Diode (asymmetric exp, 11 pts), Fold (triangle fold x2, 13 pts linear), Sine (`sin(pi x/2)`, 9 pts), Triangle (zigzag, 9 pts linear), Expo (`sgn(x)(e^{3|x|}-1)/(e^3-1)`, 9 pts smooth), Custom (no-op). Asymmetric presets (Tube, Diode) are only audible as designed with `shaperSymmetry = Asymmetric` (Ambiguity A6: library sets the symmetry parameter when generating an asymmetric preset - proposal, flagged).
- **NORMALIZE:** divide y values by max|y| of the sampled curve; **RESET:** identity (`(-1,-1),(0,0),(1,1)`, smooth).

### F. Granular Engine

**Common:** `S = min(OS, 2)` grain reads per base sample; per-oscillator engine (`GrainEngine`) with `Grain[2 channels][20]` preallocated (`struct Grain { double pos; double step; uint32 age, length; float gain; uint8 winRow; bool active, reversed; WarpState ws; }`). Output `sum_g w_g(age) * read(P_g + DeltaP_g) * gain_g` per channel, then 1/sqrt(overlap) normalisation from the window table; result up-sampled S -> OS by `OsUpsampler` (half-band IIR) **only if OS > S**. Phase-domain warps are evaluated per grain with the shared voice note clock `theta` (so `rho`, `Lc` semantics identical to Classic); amplitude-domain warps/shaper run after the grain sum at OS. The grain read pitch step = `rho * 2^(grainDetune/12)`; per-grain `ws` holds Self-FM/sync state.

**Window table:** `Wtab[33 shapes][512]` + per-shape normalisation `g(s)`, built at `prepare` (shared, read-only). `s<0.5`: attack fraction `aF = 0.02 + 0.96 s` raised-cosine attack, cos^2 release; `s=0.5`: symmetric Hann (50% overlap sums to 1); `s>0.5`: time-reversed mirror (exponential-curve attack `u^3`, sharp end). Minimum attack ramp 0.5 ms and minimum release ramp 0.5 ms always applied (never a click). Linear interpolation between shape rows.

**Scan ramp:** `t` = time since note-on (per voice, double). `D = 20 s * 0.0004^grainScan` (off below 0.001); with `SCAN KEY`: `D /= 2^((note-60)/12)`. `r = t/D` -> loop: `frac(r)`; no loop: `min(r,1)`. `scanPos = clamp(pos + dist * r, 0, 1)` (fractions of the region). Positions are latched at grain spawn (not continuously moved inside a grain), exactly as Granulator-style engines.

**Modes**
1. **CLASSIC** (2 overlapping grains per channel): hop = `size/2` output samples; each grain starts at `scanPos + var_pos`, length = `size * S*fs`, read step `rho*2^(spreadDetune/12)`; shape window; R channel schedule offset by `spread * size/4`; L/R grain detune `+-spread*30 cents`. New size takes effect at the next spawn (grain A finishes with its own length).
2. **LOOP:** one *segment* per channel: random/scan start within `var` jitter, length = `size`; two crossfading readers; crossfade length `xf = size * (0.02 + 0.48*shape)` (equal-power); next segment spawned when the active reader reaches `length - xf`; chance `grainReverse` that the new segment's step is negated (start at its end). Sounds like a crossfade-looping sample player with moving loop.
3. **CLOUD:** `grainDensity` (1-20) grains per channel, **unsynced**: initial ages uniformly distributed; each grain respawns on its own end at `scanPos + var_pos`, size jitter, transposition jitter (`+-12 var` semitones), volume jitter; fixed Hann window (`grainShape` ignored); gain `1/sqrt(N_active * 0.5)`.

**Randomness:** per-oscillator xorshift32 seeded from `(noteCounter, oscIndex, channel)` - deterministic, allocation-free, thread-private.
**Region handling:** grain positions wrap circularly inside [start,end]; `loopMode` is ignored in Granular (documented). `direction = Reverse` negates all grain steps.
**Voice-end:** grains die with the voice; ADSR release applies after the grain sum.
**CPU:** cost per oscillator per OS-sample ~ `S/OS * (2 channels * grains * ~40 flops)` => Cloud/20 grains is ~100x Classic; the oscillator budget (below) charges *grain-weighted* cost units and caps unison automatically in Granular+Cloud (Risk R2).

### G. Filter Engine: 34 Types in 9 Families

**Shared building blocks:** `TptOnePole` (LP/HP, 6 dB), `TptSvf` (12 dB, outputs LP/BP/HP/Notch/Peak/AP/Low-shelf/High-shelf via mix coefficients; reference check vs `juce::dsp::StateVariableTPTFilter`), `LadderCore` (4 x one-pole TPT with per-stage tanh and global feedback, ZDF solved by one Newton step or the Zavalishin linearised solution), `DelayComb` (Lagrange3rd `DelayLine`, capacity `fs/20 + 8`), `FormantBank` (parallel `TptSvf` bandpasses, vowel table), `AllpassChain` (1st/2nd-order TPT allpasses), `Sah` (hold counter), local 2x `HalfbandIIR` for nonlinear types. Every block exposes `response(w)` from its own coefficients (used by `FilterResponse`).

**Common controls:** `drive` = pre-filter gain `10^(dB/20)` into an ADAA1 tanh normalised by `tanh'(0)` so low drive is transparent; `cutoff` modulated + key-tracked; `mix` dry/wet; type switch = 10 ms crossfade between old and new instances (new instance state-reset, input-primed for 64 samples); per-chunk coefficient interpolation (every 8 samples). `res` 0..1 -> `Q` generally `Q = Q0 * (1 + 14 res^1.5)` on the highest-Q section (Butterworth sections otherwise fixed), clamped for stability (TPT is unconditionally stable for any Q>0).

**Analytic response (`FilterResponse::magnitudeDb`):** exact for linear types (TPT biquad-equivalent `H(z)` evaluated at 256 log-spaced points), cascade product for orders; comb exact; ladder = linearised small-signal (with `k`); Scream = BP; S&H = pre-LP curve; Ring Mod = flat with the carrier marker reflected by the cutoff guide (documented limitation). Test D5 compares the measured impulse-response FFT to the analytic curve within 0.5 dB for all linear types.

### H. Amp Envelope, Voice, Unison, Glide
- **ADSR:** state machine {Idle, Attack, Decay, Sustain, Release}. Attack linear from the **current level** to 1 over A ms; Decay/Release one-pole exponential with `tau = T/6.9`, Release ends at -90 dB -> Idle -> voice freed. Sustain changes slew 10 ms. Note-off during attack -> release from current level (no snap).
- **Unison:** `cents_i = D (2i/(N-1) - 1)` (N=1: 0); `pan_i = spread * (2i/(N-1) - 1)`, equal-power balance; output gain `1/sqrt(N)` (+ 0.3 dB/oscillator compensation tuned by test). Detune is applied to the pitch *before* `Lc`/`rho` (each oscillator is a properly detuned player).
- **Glide:** state `pitchCurrent` -> `pitchTarget` in semitones, constant-time linear ramp over `glideTime` ms; per-voice; poly voices start from the previous note's pitch.
- **Voice budget governor (opt-in knobs in Settings):** each oscillator costs `OS * c_mode` units (`c_classic=1`, `c_granular = 1 + 0.25*grains`); default budget 256 units. A new note that would exceed it first reduces **its own** unison count (never below 1), then steals. Settings can raise the cap (64-1024) or disable it. Never changes sounding voices. A "CPU guard" (off by default) additionally lowers OS for *new* notes if the 1 s EMA of block-time/budget > 85%.

### I. Modulation Engine

**Shape tables:** `LfoShapeTable` = 4096 cells x 2 values (cell start/end values) so a discontinuity can only sit on a cell boundary; built from the wire format by `LfoTableBuilder` (message thread): CUSTOM = piecewise segments with exponent `2^(3c)`; preset ids = the exact analytic functions of `v9-ui.html presetFn` converted from UI-y to wire-v (`v = 1 - y`): SINE `v=0.5+0.4 sin(2 pi t)`, TRIANGLE `0.9-0.8|2t-1|`, SAW UP/DOWN, SQUARE, PUMP, STEPS n, SWING, S&H (8-value table), DRIFT (`0.5+0.26 sin(2 pi t+a)+0.14 sin(4 pi t+b)`); preset bends = smoothstep-blended offsets over the analytic curve (anchors at 0 and 1 with dy=0), reproduced exactly. Evaluate: `v = lerp(cellStart, cellEnd, frac)`. Output `mod = 2v - 1`.

**Phase generation (`LfoEngine`):**
- `phase = frac(phase0 + phaseParam/360 + progress)` then direction mapping (Forward `p`; Reverse `1-p`; Ping-Pong: progress 0..2 -> `p` then `1-p`).
- **Hz:** `progress += rate_hz / fs` per sample. **Sync:** `beatsPerCycle` table [32,16,8,4,2,1.5,1,2/3,0.75,0.5,1/3,0.375,0.25,1/6,0.125,1/12,0.0625] for the 17 divisions ("bar" = host time-signature numerator*4/denominator beats, default 4).
- **FREE:** one global instance, never retriggered; Sync => `progress = ppq / beatsPerCycle` (grid-locked, recomputed from `ppqPosition` each block so transport jumps/loops stay locked; per-sample increments `bpm/(60 fs)/beatsPerCycle` inside the block). No transport (standalone/offline w/o playhead): internal clock at the last known bpm (default 120).
- **RETRIG:** per-voice instance reset to `phaseParam` at note-on; Sync = tempo-scaled speed (not grid-locked).
- **ENV:** per-voice, plays the shape once (rate defines duration), then holds the last value (release does not restart it).
- **MONO:** one shared instance, reset when a note starts while no other note is held; otherwise continues.
- (A1: these semantics are a proposal - the contract only says "Phase reset behaviour".)
- All LFO outputs pass a fixed 2 ms slew, then `SMOOTH` one-pole. Sources are produced **per sample** into per-source buffers (global LFOs: one buffer per block; voice LFOs: per voice per chunk), consumers interpolate: audio-rate-capable destinations (warp amount/A/B/mix, shaper morph/mix, grain params, unison, mixes) read per sample; filter coefficient destinations every 8 samples.

**TransportClock:** reads `getPlayHead()->getPosition()` once per block: `ppqPosition`, `bpm`, `isPlaying`, `timeSigNumerator/Denominator`; missing fields fall back to the internal clock; sub-block advance keyed to `Synthesiser` splits.

### J. Master, Safety, Denormals
- `juce::ScopedNoDenormals` at the top of `processBlock` (sets FTZ/DAZ incl. ARM). Recursive structures additionally add `1e-20f` alternating offsets only where FTZ is unavailable (ARM32/exotic); not needed on the supported platforms.
- **Safety:** `|x|<=0.89` untouched; above, C1-continuous knee to +-1 (`y = sgn(x)(0.89 + 0.11*tanh((|x|-0.89)/0.11))`) with ADAA1 (`F1` closed form) - bypassed bit-exactly below the knee. NaN/inf -> 0 and the offending voice is killed + flagged (debug assert in test builds).
- **DC:** 5 Hz one-pole HP at each voice decimator output and at master; asymmetric modes additionally remove analytic DC.
- **No `juce::dsp::Limiter`** anywhere (hidden fixed compressor stage, house lesson `juce_limiter_hidden_compressor`).

### K. Test Harness Rules (house lessons applied)
- Processor-level harnesses call `setPlayConfigDetails(0, 2, fs, block)` **before** `prepareToPlay` (else `getSampleRate()==0` -> NaN). No sidechain here, so the pattern-28 ordering issue does not apply (instrument has no aux buses).
- DSP-class tests call `prepare(fs, maxBlock)` explicitly and assert `fs > 0` in debug.
- Zero-allocation proof: global `operator new` hook armed during `processBlock` in `WARPR_Tests`; any allocation fails the test.

## Integration Points

### Feature Dependencies

```
SampleStore (SampleData + mips) ------------------------------------------------+
   |                                                                            |
   v                                                                            v
Classic reader / GrainEngine --(P, theta, rho)--> PhaseWarp --(P')--> SampleReader <-- ModOsc(Sample src)
   |                                                    ^                  |
   |                                                    |                  v
   |                                       ModOsc(basic shapes)       AmpWarp (ADAA) --> ShaperEngine (LUT A/B, ADAA)
   |                                                                       |
   |        ShaperEngine curve A/B  --(Phase Remapping mode 50)--> PhaseWarp
   v                                                                       v
Unison sum --> OsDecimator --> FilterEngine --> AmpEnvelope --> Voice out --> Master --> VizAnalyzer
                                   ^
LfoEngine --> ModMatrix --(per chunk)--> every V-class parameter (incl. grain position, warp, filter, ADSR, unison, LFO rate)
TransportClock -----------------------> LfoEngine (sync, grid lock)
WarprSynth (MIDI, glide, stealing) ---> Voice(pitch, velocity, note-on triggers for RETRIG/ENV LFOs, scan ramp)
UiBackendImpl <---> LfoShapeTable / ModMatrixSnapshot / ShaperLut (publish) ; SampleStore ; VizFifo ; FilterResponse
```

### Parameter Interactions
- `warpMix`, `shaperMix`, `filterMix` + their enables: independent dry/wet, ramped.
- `rootNote` participates in **both** pitch ratio and the warp cycle length `Lc` - a wrong root note changes the timbre of every phase-domain warp (documented in the UI hint by Stage 3: "set ROOT to the sample's pitch for tonal warps").
- `sampleStart/End` constrain the region used by Classic loops, Granular position domain and `RegionFold` for warped reads (`P'` outside the region is folded, not clamped, for loop modes).
- `playMode = Granular` makes `loopMode` and region-relative loops inert; `grainMode` gates which of `grainShape/grainReverse/grainDensity` are active (UI dims; DSP also ignores them).
- `shaperSymmetry` + presets (A6); `shaperMorph` interacts with Phase Remapping mode 50 only through the A param there (independent).
- `modOscSource = Sample` + `modOscRatio` + warp modes 54-59; `Self FM` ignores the modulator.
- `oversampling` multiplies CPU of the oscillator pipeline linearly; granular reads cap at 2x.
- `unisonVoices x polyphony x oversampling` is governed by the oscillator budget (R2).
- Mod destinations that are structural (polyphony, unisonVoices, glideTime) are latched at note-on.

### Processing Order Requirements
1. Block start: transport -> param snapshot -> pending publications (`LockFreeSwap` acquires) -> global LFOs -> mod matrix (global part).
2. Per sub-block (Synthesiser split) per 32-sample chunk: voice LFOs -> modulated params -> glide/pitch -> per oscillator [reader/grains -> phase offset -> read -> amp warp -> shaper -> pan/accumulate] -> decimate -> filter -> ADSR -> sum.
3. After all voices: master DC block -> gain -> safety -> analyzers -> optional viz push.
4. **Order that must not change:** `PhaseWarp` before `SampleReader` (it moves the read position); `AmpWarp` before `Shaper`; decimation before the filter; ADSR after the filter; master after the voice sum.
5. Filter-internal 2x (nonlinear types) wraps only the nonlinear core of the filter.

### Thread Boundaries

| Data | Producer | Consumer | Mechanism |
|---|---|---|---|
| Parameters | host/UI/message | audio | APVTS atomics (relaxed loads once per block) |
| SampleData (+mips, peaks) | loader worker | audio, message (peaks) | `LockFreeSwap` + ref-count + retire list |
| ShaperLut A/B (+F1) | message | audio | `LockFreeSwap` (2 slots, 10 ms audio-side crossfade) |
| LfoShapeTable x10, ModMatrixSnapshot, lfoCount | message | audio | `LockFreeSwap` each |
| Viz frames | audio | message (30 Hz timer) | `WarprVizFifo` SPSC (`AbstractFifo`, drops when full) |
| Revision counters | any | message | `std::atomic<uint32_t>` |
| Filter response | message | message | pure function of atomics + constants |
| Retired objects | audio (pushes) | message (frees) | preallocated SPSC `AbstractFifo` of raw pointers (+ extra ref) |
| Presets / state | message/host | message | synchronous in `get/setStateInformation` |
| Settings (budget, quality) | message | audio | relaxed atomics read per block |

**Forbidden on the audio thread:** allocation (`new`, `std::vector` growth, `juce::String`/`var`/`JSON`), locks, file I/O, `std::function` creation, logging. Enforced by the allocation-counting test hook and TSAN/ASAN builds (`build-tsan`, `build-asan` exist in the repo root).

## Implementation Risks

**Overall complexity:** HIGHEST in the factory. ~94 distinct algorithms (60 warp + 34 filter) + granular + mod engine + state + WebView backend, all in one plugin. Dominant risks: **CPU**, **aliasing quality**, **sheer scope**.

### R1. Aliasing (HIGH)
- **Risk:** Hard clip/folds/Chebyshev/FM/PD/sync produce strong high-order harmonics; ADAA1 and 2x may not be enough for some modes at high notes.
- **Mitigation:** Layered AA (above); per-mode alias tests (A1-A3 in plan); speed-aware mip selection; BLEP on generated steps.
- **Fallback:** (a) ADAA2 for Hard Clip/Linear Fold/Hard Fold behind a compile-time switch; (b) per-mode minimum OS hint (`minOS`: Chebyshev Harmonic 4x, Hard Fold 4x, Cross Mod 4x) that raises the effective OS for new notes (documented, shown as tooltip); (c) default OS raised to 4x.

### R2. CPU with 32 voices x 8 unison x 8x OS (HIGH, certain at the extremes)
- **Numbers (estimates, ~150 flops per oscillator per OS-sample, ~3 GFLOP/s effective single core; to be replaced by measured values in Phase D10):**

| Scenario | Oscillators x OS | Estimated load |
|---|---|---|
| Typical: 8 voices, unison 2, 2x | 16 x 2 | ~8% core |
| Heavy: 16 voices, unison 4, 4x | 64 x 4 | ~60% core |
| Extreme spec max: 32 x 8, 8x | 256 x 8 | ~5 cores - **impossible by design** |
| Granular Cloud 20 grains, unison 4, 16 voices, 2x | 64 x 2 x (~100x grain cost / Classic) | unaffordable without caps |

- **Mitigations built into the architecture:** oscillator budget (default 256 OS-units) with deterministic unison-reduction-then-steal; decimator per voice (not per oscillator); mono-source halving; `rho<=1` skips mip blend; dry read only when needed; stage-wise block processing (autovectorisable loops); 8-tap sinc dot products SIMD-friendly; OS latched per note; fast-math approximations (paired f/F1); optional Hermite4 interpolation ("Eco") in Settings; CPU guard (opt-in).
- **Fallback:** cap effective unison in Granular, lower granular `S` to 1x, halve grain counts at Cloud; ship budget defaults conservative (128) if measurements demand.

### R3. Custom polyphase IIR decimator / OS-native pipeline (MEDIUM)
- **Risk:** Our own half-band IIR cascade design/implementation error (stability, passband ripple, 8x chaining) or hidden aliasing in the "read at OS rate" assumption.
- **Mitigation:** coefficients from the public JUCE `FilterDesign` function; test D1 (impulse/sine sweep: passband <0.1 dB to 0.4 fs/2, stopband <-90 dB above 0.6 fs, per stage factor); A/B against `juce::dsp::Oversampling` on a static nonlinearity.
- **Fallback:** per-voice `juce::dsp::Oversampling<float>` used via Up -> overwrite returned block -> Down (works on JUCE 8.0.15 internals) or standard Up->nonlinear->Down for amplitude-domain modes only.

### R4. "Cycle" semantics for phase-domain warps on arbitrary samples (MEDIUM-HIGH, musical risk)
- **Risk:** Non-periodic/mis-tuned samples make PD/sync/FM sound chopped at cycle wraps; wrong rootNote -> unexpected timbre.
- **Mitigation:** `Lc` from the explicit rootNote (contract parameter); `SeamBridge`; default single-cycle wave is exactly periodic; UI hint (Stage 3).
- **Fallback:** optional auto root-note estimation on load (autocorrelation; out-of-contract suggestion, flagged only).

### R5. Granular engine quality and cost (HIGH)
- **Risk:** Clicks at spawn/size changes, level pumping, Cloud CPU, phase-domain warps per grain.
- **Mitigation:** every grain windowed with >= 0.5 ms ramps; size/position latched at spawn; normalisation LUT; preallocated pools; deterministic PRNG; per-mode tests (click metric on size sweeps).
- **Fallback:** Classic + Loop first (D7a), Cloud as D7b with reduced grain cap; per-grain phase warps limited to amplitude-domain + PM if CPU proves too high (documented per-mode degradation).

### R6. Filter bank breadth (MEDIUM, wide)
- **Risk:** Ladder/Scream/Dist LP stability under fast modulation, comb delay-modulation clicks, formant table quality, 34 response curves.
- **Mitigation:** TPT/ZDF everywhere, tanh in loops, local 2x, coefficient interpolation, crossfaded type switches, analytic-vs-measured response tests, extreme-parameter NaN sweeps.
- **Fallback:** Res LP/HP/Dist LP/Scream fall back to SVF-with-saturating-integrators (same API) if ladder solver proves fragile.

### R7. Embedded-sample state (MEDIUM)
- **Risk:** Host state size/time, FLAC writer API drift in JUCE 8.0.15, mono/stereo/bit-depth edge cases, `setStateInformation` blocking the host.
- **Mitigation:** container with size policy, codec fallback (float32 raw), synchronous decode with measured budget, state round-trip tests including 24-bit and float sources, truncated/corrupt blob fuzz tests.
- **Fallback:** zlib (`juce::GZIPCompressorOutputStream`) of float32 if FLAC writer is unusable.

### R8. WKWebView/WebView2 drag-drop (MEDIUM)
- **Risk:** WebViews swallow file drops (checklist note); drag-drop of LFO chips is in-page pointer logic (safe), file drop is native.
- **Mitigation:** native `FileDragAndDropTarget` on the editor + the always-present LOAD button (`warpr_loadSample`); test both macOS WKWebView and Windows WebView2 (house lessons: pointerup, Dock eats bottom clicks).
- **Fallback:** LOAD button as the primary path; document drop as best-effort.

### R9. 10-LFO tab strip fit (LOW-MEDIUM, UI)
- **Risk:** 10 tabs + `+` chip overflow the LFO header at the locked 1200x820 layout.
- **Mitigation:** Stage 3 checks with scoped screenshots at 3, 6, 10 tabs (checklist item); compact tab width rule (`min-width` shrink / numeric-only chips).
- **Fallback:** horizontal tab-strip scroll or two-row tabs; backend unaffected.

### R10. UI/DSP agreement for LFO shapes and shaper curves (MEDIUM)
- **Risk:** Divergent analytic formulas (`presetFn`, bends, curve exponent `2^(3c)`, Fritsch-Carlson).
- **Mitigation:** golden vectors exported from the HTML's JS functions (node script run in tests) vs C++ tables, tolerance 1e-4; shaper LUT vs UI polyline.
- **Fallback:** C++ is the authority; Stage 3 patches JS.

### R11. Voice management correctness (MEDIUM)
- **Risk:** Stuck notes with pedal + legato + stealing; glide edge cases; unison reduction on steal.
- **Mitigation:** randomized MIDI storm tests asserting all voices idle after all-notes-off; ghost fade slots; deterministic tests per mode.

### R12. Scope/schedule (HIGH)
- **Risk:** Largest plugin by an order of magnitude; "everything in 1.0" is locked.
- **Mitigation:** milestone discipline (compile+test per phase), family-shared infrastructure, algorithm tests generated per table row, each phase committed; the plan caps every phase with explicit exit criteria.
- **Fallback (scope-preserving):** ship phases in order; any mode that fails its quality gate is *fixed*, never stubbed (brief rule); schedule slip is accepted over placeholder entries.

### R13. Other
- **Windows CI/WebView2:** house lessons (FindWebView2, 64 MB stack, pluginval no-wait) apply (Low-Med).
- **Thread-safety of swaps:** TSAN run mandatory in D9 (Medium).
- **Host/AU parameter volume:** 135 parameters + `withAutomatable(false)` for 20: validate with `auval`/pluginval (Low).
- **Rename:** PLUGIN_CODE/manufacturer fixed before release; pattern #14 cleanup on PRODUCT_NAME change (Low).
- **Config drift:** relay/attachment tables generated from the single param table (Low).

**Recommended approach (risk order):** (1) infrastructure that everything depends on (param table, state container, LockFreeSwap, OS-native pipeline, Classic reader, ADSR, voices) with tests; (2) static families (bends/folds/distortion + ADAA) - validates AA strategy early; (3) shaper (LUT/F1 shares ADAA); (4) filters (independent, wide); (5) phase/sync/FM (needs reader + modulator); (6) granular (new engine on top of the reader); (7) LFO/mod (touches everything: last so parameter targets are final); (8) presets/state hardening/perf.

## Architecture Decisions

### AD1. Layered anti-aliasing
**Decision:** OS (user) + ADAA1 + BLEP + mip-mapped source. **Rationale/alternatives/tradeoffs:** see Algorithm Details A. Tradeoff: more code paths per mode (paired `f`/`F1`), accepted because it halves the OS needed for static shapers.

### AD2. Oscillator pipeline natively at the OS rate (no input up-sampler)
**Decision:** sample read, warp, shaper run at `OS*fs`; one decimator per voice. **Alternatives:** (a) `juce::dsp::Oversampling` per oscillator (256 up+down chains - rejected, CPU/memory); (b) base-rate read then up-sample (rejected: phase-domain warps would alias before up-sampling); (c) per-voice `Oversampling` object with Up-trick (kept as R3 fallback). **Tradeoff:** OS factor multiplies *all* oscillator work (read included); accepted because it's the only correct place for phase-domain AA.

### AD3. Additive read-offset formulation of phase warps
**Decision:** `P' = P + dir*Lc*Delta(theta)`. **Alternatives:** wavetable-style cycle buffers (requires known period, no sample progression), ring-buffer time-warp (adds latency of 1-3 periods, rejected for Granular). **Tradeoff:** relies on a correct `rootNote`; gives zero latency and one mechanism for Classic and Granular.

### AD4. Unison at oscillator level, filter/ADSR per note
**Decision:** as in Serum-class synths. **Alternative:** each unison voice a full voice (filter x8) - rejected on CPU. **Tradeoff:** unison voices cannot be filtered differently (accepted).

### AD5. Custom `Synthesiser` subclass, not a bespoke voice manager
**Decision:** subclass `juce::Synthesiser` (brief mandates it) for MIDI splitting; override allocation/noteOff/render. **Alternative:** own manager - more control but loses tested block splitting. **Tradeoff:** must keep global time (LFO/transport) consistent with sub-block rendering (handled in `renderVoices`).

### AD6. Binary state container with FLAC24 sample
**Decision/rationale:** see State Persistence. **Alternatives:** base64 in XML (+33%, slow), raw float32 always (3-4x larger), external file reference (violates "always reopen intact").

### AD7. Table-driven two-sided LFO shapes
**Decision:** 4096-cell, two-value tables built off-thread. **Alternatives:** evaluate analytic/point curves per sample (branchy, costly for 10 LFOs x voices), single-valued table (smears steps). **Tradeoff:** 1/4096 cycle resolution (~5 us at 50 Hz) - imperceptible.

### AD8. Own ADSR, filters, interpolation, decimator; JUCE classes where they fit
**Decision:** use JUCE for: Synthesiser, AudioFormatManager/FlacAudioFormat, APVTS, `AbstractFifo`, `DelayLine`, `FilterDesign` (coefficients), `Oversampling` (filter-internal 2x/optional), `SmoothedValue`, `StateVariableTPTFilter` (reference), `FFT` (tests). **Custom** where JUCE lacks the capability (mips, sinc reader, ADSR from level, SVF with all taps, ladder, formant, ADAA). **Not used:** `juce::dsp::Limiter` (hidden compressor), `juce::ADSR`, `juce::dsp::Oscillator`.

### AD9. OS factor latched per voice
**Decision:** applies to new notes. **Alternative:** hot-swap with state migration/clicks. **Tradeoff:** changing OS while a pad sustains does not update it until the next note (documented).

### AD10. Analytic filter response shares coefficient code with DSP
**Decision:** so the display can never lie; nonlinear types show small-signal response.

## Special Considerations

### Thread Safety
See Thread Boundaries. No `std::mutex`/`CriticalSection` in any class reachable from `processBlock`. `juce::AudioProcessorValueTreeState::Listener` callbacks may run on the audio thread (host automation): they only set atomics.

### Performance
- Per-voice scratch (preallocated in `prepareToPlay`): OS-rate stereo bus `2 x (32*8)` floats per chunk, oscillator scratch arrays ~6 x 256 floats; no per-note allocation.
- Memory (approx.): comb delay lines 34 voices x 2 ch x (fs/20+8) floats = ~2.5 MB @192 kHz; grain pools 256 osc x 40 grains x 56 B = ~0.6 MB; window table 33x512 floats; mips 2x sample size; LUT slots 2 curves x 2 x 4097 x (f + F1) floats.
- Estimated load table: see R2. Real numbers come from `WARPR_Tests --bench` in D10 (target: typical patch <15% of one core at 48 kHz/256-sample buffers on Apple M-series and a 2019 x64 laptop).

### Denormal Protection
`ScopedNoDenormals` in `processBlock`; DC blockers; feedback paths (comb, ladder, self-FM, allpass chains) clamp and add anti-denormal offset on platforms without FTZ; envelope tails terminate at -90 dB (voice freed -> no endless denormal decay).

### Sample Rate Handling
Supports 22.05-384 kHz. `prepareToPlay(fs, block)`: recompute filter coefficient generators, half-band IIR coefficients (design at `prepare`, not per note), LFO increments, comb capacity, glide/smoother lengths, mip-independent (source rate carried in `rho`). `releaseResources` leaves state valid (no frees needed). Max block size handled by chunking (any host block 1..8192+).

### Latency
Reported latency **0**. Instrument: note timing is MIDI-driven; decimator group delay (<=~1 ms at 8x) is not compensated. No look-ahead anywhere.

### Memory/Real-time init
All objects constructed in the processor constructor or `prepareToPlay`. First note after load must not allocate (test).

### Platform
macOS (VST3 + AU + Standalone) and Windows (VST3 + Standalone). Code is portable C++17 (no platform intrinsics in v1.0; SIMD via compiler autovectorisation of fixed-length loops and `juce::FloatVectorOperations`; hand intrinsics only in D10 if measurements demand).

## Contract Ambiguities Found (NOT resolved by changing contracts; the architecture states the working assumption)

| ID | Ambiguity | Working assumption in this architecture |
|---|---|---|
| A1 | `lfoNMode` Free/Retrig/Env/Mono semantics ("phase reset behaviour") undefined | FREE = single global free-run (grid-locked when synced); RETRIG = per-voice reset at note-on; ENV = per-voice one-shot then hold; MONO = one shared instance reset on first note of a phrase |
| A2 | Brief lists velocity, mod wheel, note number as mod sources; matrix wire format has `src` 1..10 only; no velocity-sensitivity or pitch-tracking-toggle parameter exists | Fixed velocity law `0.25+0.75v`; mod wheel stored, no destination; pitch tracking always on; flagged for a future contract amendment |
| A3 | Matrix `dst` = "any Float/Int knob": includes structural ints (polyphony, unisonVoices), LFO params (LFO-on-LFO), masterGain; depth is unipolar | Latching rules for structural ints, index-ordered evaluation with one-chunk delay for forward LFO references, depth 0..1 only |
| A4 | Source of the curve for "Phase Remapping" (mode 50) unspecified | Uses the shaper A/B transfer curves (A param blends A/B) even when the shaper stage is off |
| A5 | `warpParamA/B` have per-mode meaning but the UI/backend expose no per-mode labels or enable state | Compile-time `WarpModeInfo` table (labels, usesModOsc, unused knobs); Stage 3 may surface it via an extra static JSON (needs a contract amendment to the editor) |
| A6 | Shaper presets Tube/Diode are asymmetric but `shaperSymmetry` defaults to Symmetric; brief lists "invert" and "cubic" interpolation, backend has only reset/normalize and spec has `smooth|linear` | Preset library switches the symmetry parameter for asymmetric presets (proposal); no invert action; `smooth` = monotone cubic |
| A7 | Brief mentions loop start/end editing, loop crossfade, start-position randomisation, playback speed, sample gain, sample preview; spec removed most and has no separate loop points | Loop region = sampleStart/End; internal auto seam crossfade; no preview, no randomisation |
| A8 | Embedded sample size/codec cap not specified | FLAC24 (float32 raw for >24-bit sources), warning above 64 MB decoded, 10 min soft cap, first 2 channels |
| A9 | `polyphony` 32 x `unisonVoices` 8 x OS 8x is not achievable; contents of `openSettings()` unspecified | Oscillator budget + opt-in CPU guard in a native Settings dialog (non-parameter app settings) |
| A10 | `warprViz` "POST-WARP stereo bus" ambiguous | Tap = master sum after voice filters (before master gain for band energies; after safety clip for peaks) |
| A11 | Stage numbering differs across the brief, parameter-spec, checklist and plan template; "Parameter Groups" lists Global before LFO while the layout order puts LFO before Global | Plan names stages explicitly and maps them; layout order = Parameter Definitions order |
| A12 | ADSR is drawn linear in the editor; audible curve unspecified | Linear attack, exponential decay/release (-60 dB time = displayed ms) |
| A13 | Channel handling for >2-channel or 8/12-bit files unspecified | First two channels; any integer depth decoded by JUCE to float |
| A14 | Preset file format/location/extension unspecified | `.warpr` container in the user app-data folder, name from `PluginIdentity.h` |
| A15 | Built-in default wave content and root semantics unspecified | 2048-sample additive saw, root 60 = exactly one cycle per note period |
| A16 | `grainScan` exponential map, `grainVariation` sub-weights "DSP-defined/internal" | Constants given in Granular tables; tunable in D7, documented in code |
| A17 | `oversampling` is a parameter with no stated behaviour while notes sound | Latched per voice at note-on |
| A18 | `sampleStart < sampleEnd` is a contract statement but not enforced by parameter ranges; both are independently modulatable | DSP clamps with minLen = max(64 frames, 2 ms) |
| A19 | `rootNote` UI label "C3 = 60" (Yamaha convention) vs MIDI 60 | DSP uses MIDI note numbers; UI label is cosmetic |
| A20 | Brief mentions 16x oversampling "if performance allows"; spec max is 8x | 8x (spec wins) |
| A21 | `PLUGIN_CODE Wrpr` / manufacturer code are baked in `v9-CMakeLists.txt` while the name is a working title | Decide before first release (changing later orphans projects) |

## Notes
- No code was written in Stage 0. Mode constants (`E`, drive ranges, window shapes, normalisations) are starting values to be tuned by ear and by the tests in `plan.md`; the *structure* in the tables is the contract.
- Every one of the 60 warp modes and 34 filter types has an independent kernel entry in `WarpModeTable` / `FilterEngine::Type`; no placeholder entries. Any mode that fails its quality gate is a defect to fix, not an entry to hide.
